package_info.why_malicious: This package is a highly targeted supply chain attack leveraging dependency confusion. It exfiltrates host and environment information via DNS, attempts to access private registry credentials, downloads and replaces itself with a private version, exfiltrates sensitive files, and finally deploys a C2 agent capable of arbitrary code execution, file exfiltration, and system traversal. The package is designed to evade detection, clean up after itself, and maintain persistence for remote control.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: During installation, the package executes confsettingsaaa.js, which initiates the malware's first stage and enables further malicious actions.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Postinstall scripts are a common vector for malware, as they execute automatically on install.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages rarely require postinstall scripts unless for build or setup; here, it is used to launch obfuscated code.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some packages use postinstall for compiling native modules or setup.
key_indicators: Postinstall script invoking a non-standard, obfuscated file
No legitimate reason for postinstall in this context

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At installation, the code exfiltrates the username, hostname, package name, and NO_PROXY environment variable via DNS lookups to attacker-controlled subdomains, enabling stealthy reconnaissance.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Exfiltrating system and environment information via DNS is a covert data theft technique.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not exfiltrate host or environment data, especially not via DNS.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Rarely, telemetry or analytics might use DNS, but not for sensitive data.
key_indicators: Encoding of sensitive data in DNS queries

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: On error or if certain conditions are not met, the code deletes its own files, creates decoy package.json and index.js files with a misleading message, and terminates the process, performing anti-forensics and deception.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Self-deletion and decoy file creation are classic anti-forensics and evasion tactics.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate packages do not delete their own files or replace them with misleading placeholders.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Some uninstallers clean up files, but not in this deceptive manner.
key_indicators: Creates decoy files with misleading messages

execution_context.trigger: postinstall (if .npmrc with private registry credentials is found)

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At installation, if private registry credentials are found, the code downloads the private package, installs it, replaces itself, exfiltrates sensitive files (package.json, /etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf) via HTTPS POST, decrypts and launches a second-stage agent, then cleans up and exits.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Conditional logic to target only specific environments, exfiltration of sensitive files, and deployment of a second-stage agent are hallmarks of advanced targeted attacks.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal packages do not replace themselves, exfiltrate system files, or launch hidden agents.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is highly targeted and malicious.

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the agent registers with the C2 server, receives encryption keys and a UUID, then exfiltrates detailed system and environment information encrypted via HTTPS POST.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: C2 registration and encrypted exfiltration of host details are classic remote access trojan (RAT) behaviors.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Legitimate code does not register with external C2 servers or send encrypted host data.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: None; this is a hallmark of malware.
key_indicators: Encrypted exfiltration of host and environment data

malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the agent receives commands from the C2 server to execute arbitrary code, exfiltrate or download files, or delete itself, enabling full remote control and data theft.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: Remote code execution and file exfiltration on command are core RAT features.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: No legitimate package should allow remote arbitrary code execution or file exfiltration.

attack_chain.action: Postinstall script executes obfuscated wrapper (P1) on install.
Reconnaissance: Exfiltrates username, hostname, package name, and NO_PROXY via DNS to attacker.
Searches for .npmrc/private registry credentials; if not found, invokes fail function to self-delete and create decoy files.
If private registry credentials are found, downloads and installs private package, replaces itself, exfiltrates sensitive files, and launches second-stage agent.
Second-stage agent registers with C2, exfiltrates detailed system info, and enters command loop.
Agent receives and executes C2 commands: arbitrary code execution, file exfiltration, system traversal, or self-deletion.

behavioral_signatures: Postinstall script invoking obfuscated or non-standard JavaScript files
DNS lookups encoding host/user/package/environment data to external domains
Conditional logic to check for private registry credentials and bail if not found
Exfiltration of /etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf, and package.json via HTTPS POST
Decryption and execution of hidden second-stage agent
Agent registering with external C2 and supporting remote code execution
file_indicators: Decoy package.json and index.js with 'Please refer to the private registry instead of the public repo; Security Team'
Presence of ldtzstxwzpntxqn and lznfjbhurpjsqmr as dependencies
network_indicators: DNS queries to *.pkgio.com (or similar attacker-controlled domains)
C2 registration and communication to attacker-controlled IPs (DigitalOcean hosted)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor for npm packages with postinstall scripts invoking obfuscated or non-standard files. Flag DNS queries that encode host, user, or environment data to external domains. Detect exfiltration of system files (e.g., /etc/hosts, /etc/resolv.conf) via HTTPS POST to unknown domains. Look for the presence of decoy package.json/index.js files with suspicious messages. Monitor for processes that decrypt and execute hidden JavaScript agents, and for outbound connections to known C2 endpoints or domains associated with pkgio.com. Correlate the presence of suspicious dependencies (ldtzstxwzpntxqn, lznfjbhurpjsqmr) with these behaviors.
